messages:
Samir Patel: quick thought — our postmortem flow still needs a small but consistent manual step: classifying customer impact during the incident and then surfacing that to the action tracker. getting the impact label early would help prioritize follow-ups. what if the incident bot prompts the oncall with a short checklist right after page resolution?
Mia Chen: +1. we lose a lot of time later trying to recollect which customers were affected. a short checklist could be: 
- severity (sev1/sev2)
- customer-visible (yes/no)
- impacted accounts (free/prod/enterprise)
- data-loss (yes/no)
Lucy Park: love that. can we make it optional for low-sev events? don't want extra noise for paging flaps.
Samir Patel: yeah optional for sev3s and below. for sev1/2, make it required and block postmortem creation until filled.
Rajesh Iyer: technically doable. idea: IncidentBot opens a thread and posts an interactive form after the incident is closed. the form populates action tracker tags automatically.
Nora Alvarez: also add a field for customer communications sent (yes/no + link to the sent message). helps correlate follow-ups and CS handoffs.
Derek (oncall): sample flow: page triggers, we resolve, run basic RCA, IncidentBot DM -> "Classify impact" with buttons, fill minimal fields, then bot creates PM stub and attaches labels. If I'm exhausted at 3am, I can click quick options.
Samir Patel: exactly. suggested quick options: "prod-tenant-high", "prod-tenant-med", "no-customer-impact" as one-click presets.
Mia Chen: for the action dashboard, we should have a filter on those labels so ops/product can triage: "show actions from incidents with prod-tenant-high and no communication sent".
IncidentBot: [system] Created postmortem stub PM-2024-476 and added tag "awaiting-impact".
Lucy Park: small UX ask — make the bot form present in the incident thread and also DM the primary oncall so it doesn't get buried.
Rajesh Iyer: implementation notes: we can re-use the existing /incident-close hook. pseudocode: 
```
POST /hooks/incident-close {
  incident_id: 1234,
  severity: "sev2",
  primary_oncall: "derek"
}
// bot opens a modal if severity <= 2
open_modal(primary_oncall, modal_schema)
```
modal_schema could include quick-presets + free text for account list.
Nora Alvarez: timeline: can we prototype the modal + auto-tagging in 2 sprints? I'll help spec the labels and CS handoff fields.
Derek (oncall): needs to work with oncall handoff too. when rotation changes, the pending "awaiting-impact" items should be visible on the new oncall's queue. basically, the action tracker should surface unresolved impact labels per rotation.
Samir Patel: good point. add a scheduled job that rechecks open stubs and pings the current oncall at handoff times with a digest.
Mia Chen: question about data model: do we store impacted accounts as plain text or reference account ids? referencing IDs makes it easier to query. we should sync with the billing/customer db.
Rajesh Iyer: agree. we can store both: a normalized account_id list and a short free-text summary for quick reading. the bot UI will accept either.
Lucy Park: any concerns about false positives — team members mass-clicking presets and not entering details? maybe require at least a short summary for sev1/2.
Samir Patel: mandate summary for sev1/2. for sev2 maybe 10-char min.
Nora Alvarez: CS handoff process: once impact is marked, bot should optionally create a Jira ticket for CS and cc the customer success rep. add a checkbox "create CS ticket" in the modal.
Derek (oncall): also add an ephemeral "remind me" button in the modal so I can set a follow-up for later if I can't do it immediately.
IncidentBot: [system] PM-2024-476 updated: tags=[awaiting-impact, sev2], assigned_to=Derek.
Mia Chen: for the action dashboard: propose a new column under postmortem actions: "Customer Impact" (none/prod-tenant-high/enterprise-data-loss), and a boolean "CS ticket created". sorting by these should be the default for first 30 days.
Lucy Park: dashboards should also show latency of action closure vs customer impact label — high impact actions should have SLA like 7 days.
Samir Patel: let's draft the modal schema quickly here so eng can implement: 
```
fields: [
  {name: "severity", type: "radio", options: ["sev1","sev2","sev3"]},
  {name: "impact_preset", type: "select", options: ["no-customer-impact","prod-tenant-high","enterprise-data-loss"]},
  {name: "affected_accounts", type: "textarea", placeholder: "account ids or emails"},
  {name: "cs_ticket", type: "checkbox", label: "Create CS ticket and notify"},
  {name: "quick_summary", type: "text", min_length: 10}
]
```
Rajesh Iyer: implementation checklist from my side: modal UI -> hook handler -> normalize accounts -> create tags on PM -> push to action tracker -> optionally create Jira -> schedule handoff digest. estimate 8-10 days engineering work + 2 days QA.
Nora Alvarez: I'll pair with product for wording and CS ticket template.
Derek (oncall): can the bot also attach the relevant oncall runbook snippet (if any) to the PM stub? saves time.
Samir Patel: yes, we should surface runbook links and the timeline of key events automatically. IncidentBot can include the trace of commands executed (redacted) and CI deploy tags.
IncidentBot: [system] Added runbook link: https://redwood.playbooks/runbooks/ingest-backpressure
Mia Chen: security/PII note — ensure the affected_accounts field is sanitized if it contains emails; ideally we store normalized account_id and redact emails in the public PM.
Rajesh Iyer: noted. add a sanitize step before saving plain-text.
Lucy Park: last note — integration test plan: create a synthetic incident and walk through the modal -> ensure tags flow into dashboard and Jira creation is optional. add an e2e test in the incident repo.
Samir Patel: action items: 
- Rajesh: prototype modal + backend (assignment: rajesh)
- Mia & Lucy: dashboard schema + visualization (assignment: mia/lucy)
- Nora: CS ticket template + labels (assignment: nora)
- Derek: validate oncall handoff digest behavior (assignment: derek)
We should sync in 1 week with a demo. @everyone :eyes:
Nora Alvarez: I'll set up a 30-min demo time on calendar and add spec link.
IncidentBot: [system] Digest scheduled: 2049124320 - Next demo invite sent to participants.
